It depends on the University. They'll ask for all post-secondary transcripts, even if you're applying as a mature student...

I failed out of U Waterloo, and after a few years of working went back to college to get my Accounting (in reality just bookkeeping) diploma. I then was able to transfer into UWO, but only after I petitioned their initial denial of my acceptance due to low grades. And even then I only got into one of the affiliated colleges - not that I'm complaining.

So, why did you fail anyway? What was keeping you from studying?

Not sure about Canadian schools, but maybe you could get a job doing something while learning the skills for those classes. If you are a hard worker, you can get some good recommendations. Often schools want to know you're willing to work your butt off, and it'll look better than applying again right away, because they might assume nothing has changed. If you learn some of the skills before re-applying, it would be easier to get better grades because you won't have to stress about not knowing the material.

I'm not too sure about the Canadian system, but speaking from experience (I teach a class for students on critical academic probation) and from the administrators I know, a college will look more favorably on you if you were to take some time off and perhaps go to a community college for a few semesters. Once you do this (and do well) a lot of colleges will look at your past mistakes more leniently.
